svg.aria-label: Tooling head-to-head heat table: install (bun vs pnpm 12 vs yarn 4), CI-runner frozen install, pnpm 12 Rust CLI vs pnpm 10 JS, typecheck (tsgo vs tsc), build (Vite vs Next), pnpm install situations, and lint (oxlint vs ESLint); each cell shows its measured time and its multiple of the row's fastest.
svg.text: Each cell: the measured time, then its multiple of the row's fastest. 64-core host (lint: 192-core).
Install the workspace: bun, pnpm 12, yarn 4
Row label: dependency edges resolved and verified after the install. Third line: what each linker writes (node_modules entries; yarn PnP writes a 64-entry
directory and the .pnp.cjs table). Cold: no lockfile, full resolve. Warm: lockfile present, relink only. Both on a warm store. Cold store + no lockfile: fresh
store and metadata, real network; not comparable to the warm-store rows, and pnpm-isolated was not run in it. One sample per cell. pnpm 12.8.1 · bun 1.3.14 ·
CI-runner install: frozen, from the committed lockfile (1,000 apps)
Frozen install (--frozen-lockfile, --immutable, npm ci), median of 5 rotated samples, each in a fresh podman container. Same workspace shape as the 1,000-app
install rows above (11,898 dep edges). All five fail closed on lockfile drift. pnpm uses its default isolated linker. pnpm 12.8.1 · bun 1.3.14 · yarn 4.18.1 ·
Separate dataset: one workspace per leg, every leg locks the identical package set (58 packages, 1,201 importers), leg order rotated per round. Median of 3;
truly cold is one sample. Not comparable to the install rows above.
Different feature sets: Next App Router vs a Vite SPA.
pnpm 12 install situations: pnpm 12.8.1, 1,000 apps, 41,227-line lockfile
Compared down the column: each situation against the cheapest one.
ESLint runs a strict subset of oxlint's rules. oxlint is multithreaded and ESLint is not, so the ratio grows with cores (192 here). The type-aware row is
mostly tsgo vs tsc (oxlint through tsgolint, alpha). oxlint 1.86.0 · ESLint 9.39.5.
